meta.title: Outgunned by feathers: the war Australia lost to a flightless bird
meta.deck: In 1932 soldiers armed with machine guns set out to rid farmland of emus.
meta.note: 这是一篇仿《经济学人》风格的原创练习文章，不是真实外刊的转载。文中的事实是概括性描述，仅供语言学习，请不要当作引用来源。

sents.en: Outgunned by feathers: the war Australia lost to a flightless bird
sents.zh: 败给羽毛：澳大利亚输给一种不会飞的鸟的那场“战争”
notes: outgunned：火力不如对方。被一身羽毛的鸟“火力压制”，标题的反差就是笑点。
flightless：不会飞的，鸸鹋（emu）就是不会飞的大型鸟。

sents.en: In 1932 soldiers armed with machine guns set out to rid farmland of emus.
sents.zh: 1932 年，一队带着机枪的士兵出发，要把农田里的鸸鹋清除干净。
notes: armed with：配备着（武器）。
set out to do：开始着手、出发去做。
rid A of B：使 A 摆脱 B，清除 A 里的 B。

sents.en: The birds, it turned out, had other plans.
sents.zh: 结果，这些鸟另有打算。
notes: it turned out：结果发现，插在主语和谓语之间。
had other plans：另有打算，幽默地把鸟拟人化。

sents.en: After the First World War, thousands of former soldiers were given land in Western Australia and encouraged to grow wheat.
sents.zh: 第一次世界大战后，数千名退伍士兵在西澳大利亚分到土地，并被鼓励种植小麦。
notes: former soldiers：以前的士兵，即退伍军人。
were given ... and encouraged to ...：两个被动并列。

sents.en: Times were hard: prices fell during the Depression, and the government's promised subsidies never materialised.
sents.zh: 日子很艰难：大萧条期间粮价下跌，政府承诺的补贴也一直没有兑现。
notes: Times were hard：日子不好过。
the Depression：指 1930 年代的经济大萧条。
never materialised：始终没有实现。

sents.en: Then the emus arrived.
sents.zh: 接着，鸸鹋来了。
notes: 短句制造转折和悬念。

sents.en: Some 20,000 of them, migrating inland after the breeding season, found the farms irresistible: open water, cleared land and endless rows of crops.
sents.zh: 大约两万只鸸鹋在繁殖季后向内陆迁徙，发现这些农场简直无法抗拒：有水、有空地，还有一望无际的庄稼。
notes: Some 20,000：大约两万，some 放在数字前表示“大约”。
migrating inland：向内陆迁徙，现在分词作插入语。
冒号后列举三样东西解释 irresistible。

sents.en: They trampled fences, which let rabbits in, and devoured what was left.
sents.zh: 它们踩坏了围栏，让兔子钻了进来，又把剩下的庄稼吃个精光。
notes: trample：践踏、踩坏。
which let rabbits in：which 指“踩坏围栏”这件事，导致兔子进来。
devour：狼吞虎咽地吃光。

sents.en: A small military unit was dispatched, led by a major, with two machine guns and thousands of rounds of ammunition.
sents.zh: 一支小型部队被派了过去，由一名少校带领，配有两挺机枪和数千发子弹。
notes: was dispatched：被派遣。
led by a major：由一位少校率领，过去分词短语。
rounds of ammunition：发弹药，round 在这里是“一发”。

sents.en: On paper, it looked like a mismatch.
sents.zh: 从纸面上看，这根本不是一场势均力敌的较量。
notes: On paper：从纸面上、理论上看（实际未必如此）。
mismatch：实力悬殊的对抗。

sents.en: And so it proved, though not in the way anyone expected.
sents.zh: 事实果然如此，只不过和所有人想的都不一样。
notes: And so it proved：事实证明的确如此。
though not in the way ...：只是方式出乎意料，省略了 it proved。

sents.en: The emus scattered the moment the guns opened fire, splitting into small groups that were maddeningly hard to hit.
sents.zh: 机枪一开火，鸸鹋就四散奔逃，分成一小群一小群，难打得让人抓狂。
notes: the moment + 句子：一……就……。
open fire：开火。
splitting into ...：分成……，伴随动作。
maddeningly hard：难得让人发疯。

sents.en: One carefully planned ambush ended when a gun jammed with only a dozen birds down.
sents.zh: 一次精心策划的伏击，因为一挺机枪卡了壳而草草收场，只打倒了十几只鸟。
notes: ambush：伏击。
jam：（机器、枪）卡住。
with only a dozen birds down：with 结构，“只打倒了十二只”。

sents.en: Mounting a gun on a truck did not help either: the birds easily outran it over the bumpy ground, and the gunner could barely aim.
sents.zh: 把机枪架在卡车上也无济于事：在坑坑洼洼的地上，鸟轻松跑过了卡车，机枪手几乎没法瞄准。
notes: Mounting a gun on a truck：动名词短语作主语。
did not help either：也没用。
outran：outrun 的过去式，跑得比……快。

sents.en: After about a week the soldiers were withdrawn, amid mockery in the newspapers and awkward questions in parliament.
sents.zh: 大约一周后，士兵们被撤了回来，报纸一片嘲讽，议会里也有人提出了尴尬的质询。
notes: were withdrawn：被撤回。
amid ...：在……之中，后面两个名词短语并列。
awkward questions：令人难堪的问题。

sents.en: They returned soon afterwards at the farmers' request and claimed nearly a thousand kills, though the figures were disputed.
sents.zh: 不久，应农民的要求，他们又回来了，声称打死了将近一千只，不过这个数字有争议。
notes: at the farmers' request：应农民的要求。
claimed ... kills：声称击杀了……。
though ...：不过。the figures were disputed：数字受到质疑。

sents.en: Even by generous estimates, each dead bird had cost around ten bullets.
sents.zh: 即便按最宽松的估算，每打死一只鸟也要耗费大约十发子弹。
notes: by generous estimates：按宽松（偏高）的估计。
had cost：过去完成时，说到那时为止的代价。

sents.en: The officer in charge reportedly admired the emus' toughness, likening them to tanks.
sents.zh: 据说带队的军官很佩服鸸鹋的顽强，把它们比作坦克。
notes: in charge：负责的、主管的。
reportedly：据报道（之前学过）。
likening them to tanks：把它们比作坦克，伴随状语。

sents.en: The episode, now known as the Great Emu War, survives mostly as a joke.
sents.zh: 这段插曲如今被称为“鸸鹋大战”，主要作为笑谈流传下来。
notes: episode：一段插曲、事件。
now known as：如今被称为，插入语。
survives as a joke：作为笑话留存。

sents.en: Yet it carries a serious lesson about pitting brute force against a problem that is really about ecology.
sents.zh: 但它也有一个严肃的教训：用蛮力去对付一个本质上属于生态的问题，行不通。
notes: carries a lesson：带有教训。
pit A against B：让 A 和 B 对抗。
brute force：蛮力。

sents.en: In the end, what worked better was a bounty system and sturdier fences.
sents.zh: 最后，更管用的是悬赏制度和更结实的围栏。
notes: In the end：最后。
what worked better：更管用的东西，what 从句作主语。
bounty：悬赏金；sturdier：更结实的。

sents.en: Emus remain plentiful, and still wander onto farms from time to time.
sents.zh: 鸸鹋至今数量众多，时不时还会溜达到农场里。
notes: remain plentiful：依然很多。
wander onto：溜达到……上。
from time to time：时不时。

sents.en: Australia, meanwhile, has learnt to laugh about the only war it is said to have lost to a bird.
sents.zh: 与此同时，澳大利亚也学会了拿这场据说是唯一一场输给鸟的“战争”开玩笑。
notes: meanwhile：与此同时。learnt 是英式拼法。
it is said to have lost：据说输掉了，to have done 表示已经发生的事。

sents.en: The emus, characteristically, have declined to comment.
sents.zh: 鸸鹋们一如既往地拒绝发表评论。
notes: characteristically：一如既往地、典型地。
declined to comment：拒绝评论，新闻常用语，这里是幽默收尾。

vocab.zh: 火力不如对方；被比下去
vocab.note: gun（枪）+ out-（胜过）。字面是“火力被压制”，也常比喻“实力不如人”：The small shop was outgunned by the supermarket chains.

ex.en: The local team was [[outgunned]] from the start.
ex.zh: 本地队从一开始就实力不济。

ex.en: Small shops are often [[outgunned]] by big chains.
ex.zh: 小店常常被大型连锁店压着打。

vocab.note: flight（飞行）+ -less（没有）。flightless birds：不会飞的鸟，如鸵鸟、企鹅、鸸鹋。

ex.en: Penguins are [[flightless]] birds.
ex.zh: 企鹅是不会飞的鸟。

ex.en: New Zealand is home to several [[flightless]] species.
ex.zh: 新西兰有好几种不会飞的鸟。

vocab.zh: 着手、开始（做某事）；出发去
vocab.note: set out to do sth：带着目标开始做，常暗示后来结果不如预期：He set out to fix the car and ended up breaking it.

ex.en: She [[set out to]] write a novel in a month.
ex.zh: 她着手要在一个月内写完一部小说。

ex.en: We [[set out to]] find the best pizza in town.
ex.zh: 我们出发去找城里最好吃的披萨。

vocab.zh: 使 A 摆脱 B、清除
vocab.note: rid the house of mice（把房子里的老鼠清除掉）。最常用的是 get rid of（扔掉、摆脱）。过去式和过去分词都是 rid。

ex.en: We need to [[get rid of]] these old boxes.
ex.zh: 我们得把这些旧箱子扔掉。

ex.en: The new law aims to [[rid]] the streets of litter.
ex.zh: 新法律旨在清除街上的垃圾。

vocab.note: 表示事后才知道的结果：It turned out that he was right.（结果他是对的。）也可插在句中。

ex.en: [[It turned out]] the shop was closed on Mondays.
ex.zh: 结果那家店周一不开门。

ex.en: The rumour, [[it turned out]], was true.
ex.zh: 结果那个传言是真的。

vocab.note: 常用来幽默地说“事情没按计划走”：I wanted to sleep in, but my cat had other plans.（我想睡懒觉，可我的猫另有打算。）

ex.en: I wanted a quiet weekend, but my kids [[had other plans]].
ex.zh: 我想过个安静的周末，可孩子们另有打算。

ex.en: Sorry, I [[have other plans]] tonight.
ex.zh: 抱歉，我今晚另有安排。

vocab.note: 放在名词前：former president（前总统）、my former boss（我的前老板）。the former ... the latter：前者……后者。

ex.en: She met a [[former]] classmate at the station.
ex.zh: 她在车站遇到了以前的同学。

ex.en: The building is a [[former]] factory.
ex.zh: 这栋楼以前是工厂。

vocab.note: 政府给的补贴：farm subsidies（农业补贴）。动词 subsidise（补贴），形容词 subsidised（有补贴的）。

ex.en: Farmers rely on government [[subsidies]].
ex.zh: 农民依赖政府补贴。

ex.en: The [[subsidy]] keeps bus fares low.
ex.zh: 这笔补贴让公交票价保持在低水平。

vocab.note: 常用否定：The promised help never materialised.（许诺的帮助始终没来。）美式拼作 materialize。

ex.en: The pay rise we were promised never [[materialised]].
ex.zh: 答应我们的加薪始终没兑现。

ex.en: A taxi [[materialised]] out of nowhere.
ex.zh: 一辆出租车不知从哪儿冒了出来。

vocab.note: 鸟、动物季节性迁徙；人也可以：migrate to cities（迁往城市）。名词 migration。

ex.en: Many birds [[migrate]] south for the winter.
ex.zh: 很多鸟冬天往南迁徙。

ex.en: Young people are [[migrating]] to the cities.
ex.zh: 年轻人正在迁往城市。

vocab.zh: 无法抗拒的、极有诱惑力的
vocab.note: ir-（不）+ resist（抵抗）+ -ible（能……的）。an irresistible offer / smell。

ex.en: The smell of fresh bread was [[irresistible]].
ex.zh: 新鲜面包的香味让人无法抗拒。

ex.en: They made me an [[irresistible]] offer.
ex.zh: 他们给了我一个无法拒绝的条件。

vocab.note: 用脚重重地踩：trample the grass / flowers。比喻“无视、践踏”：trample on sb's rights。

ex.en: The cows [[trampled]] the vegetable garden.
ex.zh: 牛把菜园踩得一塌糊涂。

ex.en: Please don't [[trample]] the flowers.
ex.zh: 请不要踩踏花草。

vocab.note: let sb / sth in：放进来。Open the window to let in some air.（开窗透透气。）反义 keep out。

ex.en: Don't [[let in]] anyone you don't know.
ex.zh: 别让不认识的人进来。

ex.en: Open the curtains to [[let in]] the light.
ex.zh: 拉开窗帘让光线进来。

vocab.zh: 狼吞虎咽地吃光；如饥似渴地读
vocab.note: 比 eat 强烈得多：The kids devoured the pizza. 也可以说读书：She devours novels.（她看小说如饥似渴。）

ex.en: The hungry boys [[devoured]] the whole cake.
ex.zh: 饿坏了的男孩们把整个蛋糕吃光了。

ex.en: She [[devours]] a book a week.
ex.zh: 她一周就能读完一本书。

vocab.note: 派人去某处：dispatch troops / an ambulance。也指寄送：dispatch an order（发货）。

ex.en: An ambulance was [[dispatched]] at once.
ex.zh: 救护车立刻被派了过去。

ex.en: Your order will be [[dispatched]] tomorrow.
ex.zh: 您的订单明天发货。

vocab.note: 不可数。口语缩写 ammo。比喻：The report gave her critics more ammunition.（这份报告给了批评她的人更多把柄。）

ex.en: The soldiers ran out of [[ammunition]].
ex.zh: 士兵们弹药打光了。

ex.en: His mistake gave his rivals fresh [[ammunition]].
ex.zh: 他的失误给了对手新的把柄。

vocab.note: 暗示“实际情况可能不同”：On paper, the plan is perfect.（纸面上这个计划很完美。）

ex.en: [[On paper]], he is the best candidate.
ex.zh: 从纸面上看，他是最合适的人选。

ex.en: The deal looks good [[on paper]].
ex.zh: 这笔交易纸面上看起来不错。

vocab.zh: 不相配；实力悬殊的比赛
vocab.note: mis-（错）+ match（配对）。a mismatch between skills and jobs（技能和岗位不匹配）。

ex.en: The final was a complete [[mismatch]].
ex.zh: 决赛完全是一边倒。

ex.en: There's a [[mismatch]] between what we earn and what we spend.
ex.zh: 我们挣的和花的完全对不上。

vocab.note: 人群、动物四散：The crowd scattered. 也可以撒东西：scatter seeds（撒种子）。

ex.en: The pigeons [[scattered]] when the dog ran up.
ex.zh: 狗一跑过来，鸽子就四散飞走了。

ex.en: Toys were [[scattered]] all over the floor.
ex.zh: 玩具撒得满地都是。

vocab.note: = as soon as：I knew the moment I saw her.（我一看到她就知道了。）也说 the minute。

ex.en: Call me [[the moment]] you arrive.
ex.zh: 你一到就给我打电话。

ex.en: [[The moment]] I sat down, the phone rang.
ex.zh: 我刚一坐下，电话就响了。

vocab.note: open fire on sb / sth：向……开火。cease fire：停火。

ex.en: The soldiers [[opened fire]] on the target.
ex.zh: 士兵们向目标开火。

ex.en: Don't [[open fire]] until I say so.
ex.zh: 我不下令就别开火。

vocab.zh: 令人恼火地、让人抓狂地
vocab.note: madden（使发疯）+ -ingly。maddeningly slow（慢得让人抓狂）。

ex.en: The internet was [[maddeningly]] slow.
ex.zh: 网速慢得让人抓狂。

ex.en: The instructions were [[maddeningly]] vague.
ex.zh: 说明书含糊得让人恼火。

vocab.note: 名词和动词同形：set up an ambush（设下埋伏），be ambushed（遭到伏击）。比喻：记者在门口“堵人”也叫 ambush。

ex.en: The soldiers walked into an [[ambush]].
ex.zh: 士兵们中了埋伏。

ex.en: Reporters [[ambushed]] him outside his house.
ex.zh: 记者们在他家门口堵住了他。

vocab.note: The printer jammed again.（打印机又卡纸了。）名词 traffic jam（交通堵塞），paper jam（卡纸）。

ex.en: The door [[jammed]] and wouldn't open.
ex.zh: 门卡住了，打不开。

ex.en: The printer [[jams]] every time I use it.
ex.zh: 我每次用打印机它都卡纸。

vocab.note: mount a TV on the wall（把电视挂到墙上）。也可指组织活动：mount a campaign（发起运动）。

ex.en: We [[mounted]] the TV on the wall.
ex.zh: 我们把电视挂到了墙上。

ex.en: A camera was [[mounted]] above the door.
ex.zh: 门上方装了一个摄像头。

vocab.note: out-（胜过）+ run。过去式 outran，过去分词 outrun。比喻：Demand has outrun supply.（需求超过了供应。）

ex.en: You can't [[outrun]] a cheetah.
ex.zh: 你跑不过猎豹。

ex.en: The thief [[outran]] the police officer.
ex.zh: 小偷跑得比警察还快。

vocab.note: bump（隆起、碰撞）+ -y。a bumpy road / flight。比喻：a bumpy start（开局不顺）。

ex.en: It was a [[bumpy]] ride over the mountains.
ex.zh: 翻山的路一路颠簸。

ex.en: The new shop had a [[bumpy]] first year.
ex.zh: 这家新店头一年开得磕磕绊绊。

vocab.note: withdraw troops（撤军），withdraw from a race（退出比赛）。过去式 withdrew，过去分词 withdrawn。

ex.en: The army [[withdrew]] from the city.
ex.zh: 军队撤出了这座城市。

ex.en: She [[withdrew]] from the competition.
ex.zh: 她退出了比赛。

vocab.note: 动词 mock（嘲笑）。make a mockery of sth：使……显得可笑、成为笑柄。

ex.en: His speech drew [[mockery]] online.
ex.zh: 他的演讲在网上招来一片嘲讽。

ex.en: The trial made a [[mockery]] of justice.
ex.zh: 这场审判简直是对正义的嘲弄。

vocab.zh: 尴尬的、令人难堪的；不灵活的
vocab.note: an awkward silence（尴尬的沉默），an awkward question（让人难堪的问题）。

ex.en: There was an [[awkward]] silence after his joke.
ex.zh: 他讲完笑话后是一阵尴尬的沉默。

ex.en: She asked me an [[awkward]] question.
ex.zh: 她问了我一个让人难堪的问题。

vocab.note: at the request of sb / at sb's request。request 作名词：make a request（提出请求）。

ex.en: The song was played at my [[request]].
ex.zh: 这首歌是应我的要求放的。

ex.en: The meeting was moved at the [[request]] of the staff.
ex.zh: 应员工要求，会议改了时间。

vocab.note: dispute 作动词：对……提出异议；名词：争端。a disputed border（有争议的边界）。

ex.en: The result is still [[disputed]].
ex.zh: 结果仍有争议。

ex.en: They [[dispute]] the official figures.
ex.zh: 他们对官方数字提出质疑。

vocab.note: by some estimates（据某些估计），by conservative estimates（保守估计），by generous estimates（按宽松的估计）。

ex.en: By some [[estimates]], half the shops will close.
ex.zh: 据某些估计，一半的店会关门。

ex.en: By conservative [[estimates]], the repairs will take a year.
ex.zh: 保守估计，维修要花一年。

vocab.note: the person in charge（负责人），be in charge of sth（负责某事），take charge（接管）。

ex.en: Who's [[in charge]] here?
ex.zh: 这里谁负责？

ex.en: She is [[in charge]] of the marketing team.
ex.zh: 她负责营销团队。

vocab.note: liken 比 compare 更书面：He likened the city to a giant maze.（他把这座城市比作一座巨大的迷宫。）

ex.en: She [[likened]] the job to running a marathon.
ex.zh: 她把这份工作比作跑马拉松。

ex.en: Critics [[likened]] the film to a dream.
ex.zh: 评论家把这部电影比作一场梦。

vocab.zh: 使 A 与 B 对抗
vocab.note: pit 作动词：让双方较量。The match pits the champion against a newcomer.（这场比赛让卫冕冠军对阵新人。）

ex.en: The final [[pitted]] two old rivals against each other.
ex.zh: 决赛让两个老对手狭路相逢。

ex.en: The game is about [[pitting]] your wits against the computer.
ex.zh: 这个游戏就是和电脑斗智。

vocab.note: brute（野兽般的）+ force（力量）。by brute force：靠蛮力。编程里 brute force 指“暴力破解”。

ex.en: He opened the jar by [[brute force]].
ex.zh: 他靠蛮力把罐子拧开了。

ex.en: [[Brute force]] won't solve this puzzle.
ex.zh: 蛮力解不开这道谜题。

vocab.note: a bounty on sth（对……的悬赏）。bounty hunter：赏金猎人。也表示“丰盛”：the bounty of the harvest。

ex.en: The town offered a [[bounty]] for every rat caught.
ex.zh: 镇上每抓到一只老鼠就给赏金。

ex.en: There is a [[bounty]] on his head.
ex.zh: 有人悬赏要他的人头。

vocab.note: sturdy shoes / table / fence：结实的鞋 / 桌子 / 围栏。比较级 sturdier。

ex.en: Buy a [[sturdy]] pair of boots for the hike.
ex.zh: 买双结实的靴子去徒步。

ex.en: We need a [[sturdier]] table.
ex.zh: 我们需要一张更结实的桌子。

vocab.note: wander around the town（在城里闲逛）。也指思绪走神：My mind wandered.

ex.en: We [[wandered]] around the old town all afternoon.
ex.zh: 我们在老城区逛了一下午。

ex.en: Don't let the children [[wander]] off.
ex.zh: 别让孩子们走丢了。

vocab.note: be said to do：据说（现在）……；be said to have done：据说（以前）做过……。The castle is said to be haunted.（据说城堡闹鬼。）He is said to have met the Queen.（据说他见过女王。）

ex.en: The house [[is said to have]] belonged to a famous painter.
ex.zh: 据说这栋房子曾属于一位著名画家。

ex.en: The lake [[is said to be]] bottomless.
ex.zh: 据说这个湖深不见底。

vocab.conn: 主语 + be said to do（现在）/ to have done（过去）
vocab.say: the only war it is said to have lost to a bird

pick.q: The tree is said ___ over 500 years old.
pick.why: 说的是树现在的年龄，用 be said to be。

pick.q: Shakespeare is said ___ in this inn.
pick.why: 说的是过去的事（莎士比亚曾住过），用 to have done。

vocab.note: characteristic（特点）+ -ally。表示“正如其一贯作风”：He was, characteristically, late.（他一如既往地迟到了。）

ex.en: She replied, [[characteristically]], with a joke.
ex.zh: 她一如既往地用一个笑话作答。

ex.en: The weather was [[characteristically]] grey.
ex.zh: 天气一如既往地灰蒙蒙的。

breakdown.en: The emus scattered the moment the guns opened fire, splitting into small groups that were maddeningly hard to hit.
points: 主干：The emus scattered —— 鸸鹋四散奔逃。
the moment the guns opened fire：一……就……，the moment 相当于 as soon as，引导时间状语。
splitting into small groups：现在分词表示同时发生的动作，“分成小群”。
that were maddeningly hard to hit：定语从句修饰 groups，hard to hit = 很难打中，maddeningly 加强语气。
